title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leak and Bronchopleural Fistula in Children: A Systematic Review of Indications, Procedural Approaches, and Outcomes.
authors: Mahindrakar N, Bhandari P, Yedatore R, Vorakunthada Y, Lilitwat W
abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent air leak (PAL) and bronchopleural fistula (BPF) are uncommon but important complications in children, particularly with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative injury, malignancy, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). When conservative therapy fails or surgery is high-risk, endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement has emerged as a minimally invasive bronchoscopic option. This systematic review summarizes the published pediatric experience, focusing on indications, procedural approach, and outcomes. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2026, with Google Scholar and reference lists screened; no language limits applied. Eligible studies reported pediatric or late-adolescent patients who underwent bronchoscopic valve placement for PAL, BPF, or pneumothorax with ongoing air leak. Case reports, case series, and observational studies with extractable pediatric data were included. Two reviewers independently screened, assessed eligibility, and abstracted data; findings were synthesized narratively. RESULTS: Thirteen reports were included. Valve placement achieved rapid or eventual air-leak improvement in selected children, including those with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative air leak, chronic ventilator dependence, malignancy, and ECMO support. Reported complications included valve migration or loosening, granulation tissue, minor hemoptysis, atelectasis, contralateral pneumothorax, and recurrent air leak, although many children underwent valve removal without complication. CONCLUSION: Endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement may be a useful rescue or bridge therapy for carefully selected children with refractory PAL or BPF. Evidence remains low certainty owing to small samples, retrospective design, inconsistent outcome definitions, and possible publication bias. Prospective multicenter registries with standardized reporting are needed to define optimal selection, timing, and safety.

title: Sex-dependent habenular dysregulation across the continuum of stress exposure and depression severity: A systematic review of preclinical and clinical evidence.
authors: Ferreira-Vorkapic C, Coelho RR, Wiech M, Tocco F, Todde F
abstract: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is diagnosed at roughly twice the rate in women as in men, yet sex is still routinely treated as a covariate rather than a biological variable of primary interest in depression research. The habenula (Hb), particularly the lateral habenula (LHb), is an increasingly implicated substrate of depression, but two recent systematic reviews found sex-stratified habenula data sparse and reported sex effects inconsistent in direction. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether sex-related effects on habenula structure and function are patterned by stress intensity or chronicity in preclinical models, and by depression severity or chronicity in clinical populations, rather than arbitrary. METHODS: This review builds on two parent systematic reviews (Cameron, Weston-Green and Newell, 2024; Fortin et al., 2025), extracting eligible sex-stratified studies and supplementing them with an independent, two-phase search (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) for comprehensive coverage of sex- and stress-related terms. Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by stressor chronicity (preclinical) and illness chronicity or severity (clinical), without meta-analysis. RESULTS: Seventeen studies met eligibility criteria (10 preclinical, 7 clinical). In preclinical models, acute stressors produced modality-dependent, sometimes opposite-direction sex effects, while chronic stressors more consistently interacted with, and sometimes abolished, pre-existing baseline sex differences. In clinical populations, sex-dependent habenula abnormalities were largely absent in first-episode presentations and became more pronounced, often specifically in women, with greater illness chronicity, treatment resistance, or symptom severity. CONCLUSIONS: Sex-dependent habenula dysfunction in depression shows a patterned, chronicity-linked structure in both literatures, though the evidence base remains small and several conclusions rest on a single study. These findings are hypothesis-generating rather than establishing sex as a confirmed driver of habenula dysfunction. Estrous cycle stage, baseline circuit-level sexual dimorphism, and sociocultural confounds are identified as testable moderators for future research.

title: Artificial Intelligence in suicide prevention: promise, peril, and clinical implications for clinical practice.
authors: Nobile B, Courtet P
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry is progressing rapidly, with promising yet underexplored applications in suicide prevention. While most existing studies have focused on suicide risk prediction, AI could be applied more broadly across the suicide prevention continuum. This review explores AI's potential in improving the detection of suicidal ideation (SI), enhancing clinician training, and expanding patient access to psychotherapeutic support. Studies suggest that AI models may identify SI more sensitively than clinicians by detecting subtle linguistic or semantic cues. Furthermore, AI-based virtual patients have been shown to improve clinicians' confidence and accuracy in suicide risk assessments, particularly when used alongside traditional training methods. On the patient side, CBT-inspired AI tools offer scalable, on-demand support, but most remain unregulated and clinically unvalidated. Despite their perceived empathy and availability, such tools pose ethical and clinical risks. Many patients use AI tools without professional guidance, a trend clinicians often underestimate. This disconnect calls for urgent regulatory oversight and professional engagement. Without clear clinical validation, AI-based tools may evolve outside medical frameworks, exposing vulnerable individuals to preventable harm. Psychiatry must not only adapt but also lead, ensuring that innovation is harnessed responsibly to serve patients with empathy, safety, and scientific rigor.

title: Maternal diet and offspring ASD and ADHD: A critical narrative review of dietary patterns, choline, and polyphenol-related exposures.
authors: Alalwan TA, Perna S
abstract: Maternal diet may influence fetal neurodevelopment through nutrient availability, placental function, and maternal-fetal metabolite signaling. This critical narrative review used a structured, purposive search to organize human evidence on prenatal dietary patterns, choline, and polyphenol-related exposures according to outcome directness: diagnosed autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), related dimensional traits, and general neurodevelopment. Whole-diet studies provide the most direct human evidence, but diagnostic findings are cohort-dependent and vulnerable to residual familial and genetic confounding. Choline trials and cohorts mainly address attention-related traits or general cognition; they do not establish prevention of diagnosed ASD or ADHD. Polyphenol evidence is limited to food proxies and one trimester-specific cohort of estimated intake, without diagnostic or biomarker-based studies. Preclinical data support biological plausibility-particularly for choline in BTBR, maternal immune-activation/CHRNA7, and Ts65Dn models and for resveratrol in valproate-exposed rodents-but remain model-specific. The evidence is therefore best treated as an organizing framework rather than a confirmed causal hypothesis. Clinical translation should prioritize achieving recommended dietary adequacy and balanced dietary patterns; evidence does not support high-dose single-nutrient or concentrated-polyphenol supplementation for ASD/ADHD prevention.

title: Contraception during the transition to menopause: a commentary.
authors: Versailles JBE, Bahamondes L, Grandi G, Juliato CRT
journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The transition to menopause presents unique clinical challenges, requiring a balance between pregnancy prevention and the management of perimenopausal symptoms and age-related comorbidities. Although fertility declines with advancing age, unintended pregnancy after age 40 remains possible and is associated with increased maternal and neonatal risks. Women who wish to avoid pregnancy need effective contraception until menopause is established. OBJECTIVE: To provide practical guidance on contraceptive counselling during the transition to menopause, considering the safety, effectiveness, noncontraceptive benefits, and limitations of available contraceptive methods. RESULTS: Age alone is not a contraindication to any contraceptive method; however, the higher prevalence of cardiovascular, metabolic, and malignant conditions in this population requires individualised contraceptive counselling based on each woman's medical history, preferences, reproductive goals, and shared decision-making. Contraceptive care in midlife is more complex than pregnancy prevention alone. Contraceptive counselling should consider both the likelihood of user adherence and the noncontraceptive benefits of each method. CONCLUSION: This commentary provides practical guidance on contraceptive counselling during the transition to menopause, reviewing the safety, effectiveness, noncontraceptive benefits, and limitations of both short-acting reversible contraceptives (SARCs) and long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) to support informed, individualised contraceptive care.

title: Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.
authors: Guo H, Jiang Y, Li D, He K, Chen Y, Li Y, Dai S, He Y
abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is a major pathogen responsible for adverse perinatal outcomes; rapid and accurate detection is crucial for preventing maternal-neonatal transmission and for guiding clinical interventions. Current GBS detection methods are limited by long assay times, insufficient sensitivity, and high equipment and operational requirements, restricting their application in resource-limited settings and rapid detection scenarios. Targeting the cfb gene of GBS, this study developed ERA-CasMNPs by integrating enzymatic recombinase amplification (ERA), CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated specific recognition and trans-cleavage activity of ssDNA, and horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-modified magnetic nanoparticle complexes (MNPs)-based colorimetric signal output. The ERA-CasMNPs biosensor enables rapid and sensitive visual detection of GBS within 85 min, with an LOD95 of 23.3 copies/μL (95% confidence interval: 15.6-34.8 copies/μL). Moreover, evaluation using 135 cultured clinical bacterial isolates demonstrated that ERA-CasMNPs achieved a sensitivity of 97.33%, a specificity of 98.33%, and a detection accuracy of 97.78%, comparable to qPCR. These results indicate that the ERA-CasMNPs biosensor provides a sensitive and visual method for rapid detection of GBS and supports its potential for further evaluation in resource-limited and rapid-testing settings.

title: Atypical early-life ultrasonic vocalizations disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad in the BTBR model of autism spectrum disorder.
authors: Cofsky NI, Binder MS
abstract: Alterations in early-life communication are a defining feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). While these deficits are well conserved in mouse models, few studies have assessed how aberrations in neonatal vocalizations affect maternal behaviors and disrupt the pup-dam communication dyad. To better elucidate the consequences of altered communication in ASD models, we assessed ultrasonic vocalization (USV) production in pups and the corresponding retrieval behaviors in dams using C57 and BTBR (autistic-like) mice. We first used the pup's dam as the retriever and found that BTBR dams retrieved significantly fewer pups than C57 dams. We then used a novel C57 dam as the retriever and found that BTBR pups were retrieved significantly slower than C57 pups. Follow-up analyses detected positive correlations between call duration and retrieval time and amplitude and retrieval time in BTBR pups. Similarly, we found that C57 mice that were retrieved the fastest had calls of a lower amplitude than slowly retrieved mice. In the BTBR model, we found that faster retrieved mice produced shorter calls with a higher pitch than slowly retrieved mice, displaying call characteristics more similar to C57 pups. Lastly, we found that a more diverse call type repertoire was associated with a faster retrieval time. Overall, our study demonstrates that altered USV production significantly affects the pup-dam communication dyad. Furthermore, we identified the USV duration, amplitude, and a more diverse call type repertoire as being critical factors underlying maternal retrieval.

title: Postoperative infections after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass - incidence, performance of diagnostic procedures, and predictive factors.
authors: Erixon C, Johannesson E, Dardashti A, Melhammar L, Nilsson J, Thelaus L, Linder A, Zindovic I
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cardiac surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) induces a systemic inflammatory response that affects common inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell count (WBC), and body temperature, complicating postoperative diagnosis of infections. The objective of this study was to assess the incidence of postoperative infections and evaluate the performance of clinically used biomarkers. DESIGN: This was a bidirectional cohort study including patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB between 1st of February 2020 and 22nd of September 2021. Patients with postoperative infection were compared to patients without. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative infections. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated the diagnostic ability of current biomarkers to detect infection. RESULTS: A total of 1,222 patients were included. The incidence of postoperative infections (during hospitalisation and/or late infection) was 17.3%. Patients with postoperative infection had more comorbidities, underwent more complex procedures, and had higher mortality (90-day mortality 3.8% vs 1.5%, p = 0.045; 1-year mortality 5.7% vs 2.7%, p = 0.032). CRP, WBC, and temperature performed poorly in detecting postoperative infection, although peak CRP (OR 1.069, p < 0.001) and peak temperature (OR 2.408, p = 0.005) were independent predictors of postoperative infection. Peak temperature occurred on postoperative day 5 in infected patients versus day 2 in those without infection. CONCLUSION: Postoperative infections following cardiac surgery with CPB remain common and are associated with increased postoperative complications and mortality. Common inflammatory biomarkers perform poorly in detecting infection. Improved diagnostic tools are needed to facilitate early detection and treatment.

title: Causal discovery from nonstationary subsample time series.
authors: Chen W, Huang Q, Wang F, Hao Z, Cai R
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Causal discovery from nonstationary subsample time series is a fundamental yet challenging problem in many scientific domains. In such data, observations are often recorded at a coarse time scale (subsampling). At the same time, the underlying data-generating mechanisms may change over time (nonstationarity), making standard methods that assume a single, fixed causal model unreliable. To address these challenges, we propose a local-to-global causal graph reconstruction framework for nonstationary subsample time series. Specifically, we first identify key latent variables via a pure-child-anchored strategy to recover boundary structures. We then infer contemporaneous causal relations through one-sided reduction and redundant-edge elimination. Finally, we reconstruct the full-time causal directed acyclic graph using recursive blocking and coefficient-invariant transfer, enabling consistent integration across nonstationary segments. We further provide theoretical guarantees for the correctness of the proposed method under mild conditions. Extensive experiments on synthetic datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in recovering the underlying causal structure under both subsampling and nonstationarity. Moreover, an application to the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset reveals interpretable, stage-dependent causal pathways from mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to Alzheimer's disease (AD), highlighting the practical utility of our approach.

title: Adolescent social isolation drives sex-dependent shifts in medial prefrontal cortex endocannabinoid tone and excitatory/inhibitory balance: the protective role of a methyl donor.
authors: Ricciardi F, Mosca L, Belardo C, Bonsale R, Fusco A, Teweldemedhin MM, Piscitelli F, di Marzo V
abstract: Prolonged social isolation triggers neuropsychiatric impairments linked to brain neurotransmitter imbalances. This study investigated the impact of social isolation on sensory perception, affective states, and the levels of amino acid neurotransmitters and endocannabinoids within the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of both male and female adolescent mice. Furthermore, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), a methyl donor with established antidepressant properties, in mitigating these alterations. Single-housed (SH) male mice developed mechanical allodynia, cold hyperalgesia, depression-like behavior, and general malaise, alongside significantly decreased GABA levels in the mPFC. SAMe treatment effectively ameliorated these symptoms, restoring GABAergic tone and increasing glycine and glutamate levels. In contrast, SH female mice exhibited anxiety-like behavior and pain hypersensitivity without depression-like traits. Their neurochemical profile was characterized by decreased GABA but increased levels of glutamate and specific endocannabinoids/acylethanolamides (2-AG, PEA, and LEA) in the mPFC. In females, SAMe treatment successfully reversed anxiety-like behavior and pain hypersensitivity, normalized glutamate, LEA, and GABA levels, and increased glycine and DHG. Our findings demonstrate that while social isolation-induced neuropsychiatric and neurochemical alterations are sex-dependent, the development of sensory hypersensitivity and the therapeutic responsiveness to SAMe are consistent across sexes. By restoring GABAergic homeostasis and modulating excitatory and endocannabinoid signaling in the mPFC, SAMe emerges as a promising pharmacological intervention for treating the complex psychiatric and sensory sequelae induced by chronic social stress.

title: Children's health before, during, and after parental/caregiver immigration detention in the United States: findings from a cross-sectional survey.
authors: Thapa K, Patler C, Saadi A
abstract: BACKGROUND: Parental immigration detention is a significant yet understudied stressor with potential consequences for children's well-being. We examined children's general health before, during, and after parental detention, and compared to the United States (US) pediatric population. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional household telephone survey in 2022-2023 of family members of immigrants detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in 2020/21 and released on bond. Of 88 respondents, we analyzed data from 49 families with at least one school-aged minor child. Family members retrospectively reported on child health before, during, and after detention using the 7-item parent-report version of the PROMIS® Parent Proxy Scale- Global Health 7 measure, which provides standardized T-scores (mean = 50, SD = 10) benchmarked to the U.S. general population. FINDINGS: The mean T-scores were statistically equivalent to the population mean of 50 at pre-detention (49; 95% CI: 46.0, 52.0) and after release (48.9; 95% CI: 45.5, 52.4) but 17 T-score points (∼2 SD below the population mean) lower during detention (31.8; 95% CI: 28.6, 35.0), substantially exceeding the commonly accepted 5 T-score points threshold (half-SD) for clinically meaningful change. Reported problems for children during parental detention included decline in grades (n = 34, 69%), increased financial responsibilities (n = 29, 59%), household or caregiving responsibilities (n = 26, 53%), and food insecurity (n = 26, 53%). About 16% (n = 8) of children were unable to receive needed treatment or counseling from a mental health professional during parental detention. INTERPRETATION: Parental detention was associated with poorer reported child health, and reported health scores improved after release. Findings highlight the need for policies that consider the health consequences of immigration enforcement on children and families. FUNDING: This research was supported by the National Science Foundation and the Russell Sage Foundation and the Carnegie Corporation of New York.

Influence of perineal tears and body image disturbance on postpartum sexual quality of life: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Fillion D, Ruffolo AF, Verlet N, Martin C, Garabedian C, Rubod C, Kerbage Y, Cosson M
journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether perineal injury severity independently determines postpartum sexual quality of life (SQoL) is unclear. This study evaluated perineal tears and body image as determinants of SQoL and sexual resumption timing. METHODS: A total of 173 women (2-24 months postpartum, vaginal delivery) completed an online questionnaire including the SQoL-F and Body Image Scale (BIS). Women with perineal tear/episiotomy (PT/E; n = 118) were compared with those with an intact perineum (n = 51) using multivariate regression. RESULTS: SQoL-F scores were similar between groups (71.1 ± 23.3 vs 76.9 ± 24.0; p = 0.10), though PT/E delayed sexual resumption (p = 0.04). On multivariate analysis, SQoL-F was independently associated with dyspareunia (β = -10.96; p < 0.001), body image disturbance (β = -0.93; p < 0.001), and pre-pregnancy sexual satisfaction (β = +4.99; p = 0.001), but not tear type. Delayed resumption was independently associated with OASI (OR = 7.02; p = 0.02), first/second-degree tears (OR = 2.20; p = 0.04), and lower pre-pregnancy relationship satisfaction (OR = 0.50; p = 0.048). CONCLUSIONS: Postpartum SQoL is primarily determined by dyspareunia and body image disturbance rather than perineal tear severity. OASI carries a substantial risk of delayed sexual resumption, warranting dedicated postpartum counseling.

title: "Sailing Two Boats" the fragmented identity of working women and the hidden labor of infertility: a qualitative analysis.
authors: Dhar S, Poojari VG, Adiga P, Mundkur A, Tomar A, Kumar P
journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To explore how professional women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART) experience and manage conflicts between treatment demands and professional identity; and to identify ways healthcare professionals can support them. METHODS: Following COREQ guidelines, semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 18 professional women undergoing ART in a tertiary care hospital. Reflexive Thematic Analysis bolstered by interdisciplinary investigator triangulation (clinical and basic science) ensured thematic confirmability. RESULTS: Analysis revealed Gendered Occupational Asymmetry (female occupational burden regardless of clinical aetiology), the Insider Paradox (the role reversal for healthcare professionals) and the Workplace Panopticon (constant self-surveillance to preserve professional authority). Interestingly, work simultaneously often acted as a Sanctuary of Competence, providing psychological respite. Finally, narratives exposed an Existential Rumination (mourning past personal-professional decisions) and permanent temporal career stalling. These themes were further mapped onto a 'A Day in the Life' structural framework to illustrate compounding daily burdens. CONCLUSIONS: Current clinical lifestyle directives inadequately account for the rigid psycho-socioeconomic structures governing professional women. Based on identified themes, we propose targeted measures for healthcare professionals to deliver patient-centric care by integrating occupational awareness and identity-sensitive counselling into routine ART practice, thereby potentially reducing distress and improving treatment experience.

title: Maternal piromelatine treatment is associated with attenuated behavioral alterations and sex-specific changes in hippocampal pCREB/BDNF signaling in adult offspring following prenatal constant-light exposure.
authors: Stoyanova T, Ivanova P, Tchekalarova J
abstract: Maternal exposure to constant light during pregnancy (CLE) is associated with disrupted circadian organization and persistent behavioral alterations in adult offspring. This study examined behavioural performance and 24-hour locomotor activity patterns, as well as hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels, in adult male and female offspring following prenatal CLE and maternal treatment with piromelatine (pir), which acts as an agonist at melatonin MT1/MT2 and serotonin 5-HT1A/5-HT1D receptors. Pregnant Wistar rats under light-dark regime received vehicle (veh), whereas dams exposed to CLE received vehicle (LL-veh), pir (10 mg/kg), or melatonin. Compared to the LL-veh groups, offspring from pir-treated dams exhibited reduced anxiety- and depression-like responses and improved working memory in both sexes. Individual-subject cosinor analysis revealed heterogeneous 24-hour locomotor rhythmicity within and between groups. No significant treatment-group effect was detected for MESOR or amplitude, and the descriptive acrophase patterns did not provide evidence of treatment-induced restoration or normalization of circadian organization. Maternal pir treatment was associated with higher hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels in male, but not female offspring relative to the LL-veh group. While the behavioral and molecular differences occurred concurrently in males, these findings do not prove that pCREB/BDNF signaling mediated the behavioral outcomes. Furthermore, the study cannot distinguish the direct developmental effects of maternal pir exposure from those mediated through maternal or offspring circadian rhythm. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as long-term behavioral and sex-specific molecular differences associated with maternal pir treatment rather than as evidence of circadian-independent antidepressant, anxiolytic, cognitive-enhancing, or BDNF-enhancing actions.

title: Functional remodeling of the maternal brain: Linking brain c-Fos dynamics to behavioral changes in pregnancy: An exploratory study.
authors: Yang L, Shang Y, Liu X, Wang J, Zhang H, Yang L
abstract: As an exploratory study with a limited sample size, this work systematically examined pregnancy-induced changes in neural activity by analyzing c-Fos expression across the whole brain of pregnant mice. The results showed that 36 brain regions-including the cortex, hippocampus, thalamus, and hypothalamus-exhibited dynamic changes in c-Fos expression throughout pregnancy. Behavioral tests revealed that pregnant mice displayed increased anxiety-like behavior in the elevated plus maze. Group-level descriptive correlation analysis indicated nominal directional trends between regional c-Fos expression and anxiety-related behavior, but no associations remained statistically significant after multiple testing correction. Furthermore, comparison with human prenatal brain imaging data suggested that adaptive changes in the hippocampus and hypothalamus are conserved across species. These preliminary findings provide initial insights into understanding brain adaptation during pregnancy, and require validation in larger cohort studies.

title: Hemodynamic effects of ventilating or not, during cardiopulmonary bypass in a porcine model.
authors: Kvalheim VL, Mongstad A, Husby P, Stangeland L, Nginamau ES, Osman TA, Yamada S, Grong K
abstract: Background. Optimal ventilator setting during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is unknown. Improved gas exchange and lung compliance have been suggested as favourable outcomes when lungs are ventilated. However, long-time effects have been hard to demonstrate. There has been less focus on the immediate circulatory effects of ventilator settings during cardioplegia and CPB, and potentially hemodynamic effects of different ventilator strategies are unknown. Methods. Sixteen anesthetized pigs on normothermic CPB with 80 min of aortic cross-clamp and cardioplegic arrest were randomized to a ventilated and a not ventilated group. After weaning, both cardiac-, hemodynamic-, and pulmonary functions were evaluated for up to 120 min. Results. Left ventricular variables and cardiac output did not differ between the two study groups, neither before nor after weaning. After weaning, mean pulmonary artery pressure was increased in ventilated compared to not ventilated animals. Neither pulmonary compliance nor oxygen uptake differed between groups in surviving animals. Conclusions. Disconnection of the ventilator during CPB and cardiac arrest did not affect lung compliance and oxygen uptake, neither positively nor negatively. In the ventilated group, a temporary increase in the pulmonary pressure after weaning was observed.

title: Clinical Outcomes following invasive coronary angiography for patients with acute coronary syndromes pretreated with P2Y12 inhibitors and considered for urgent coronary artery bypass graft surgery.
authors: Lim CJ, Singh M, Sammut MA, Faizur Rahman ME, Parker WAE, Sadeque SAA, Storey RF
abstract: This retrospective single-centre observational study included 262 sequential patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) undergoing invasive coronary angiography (ICA) while receiving P2Y12 inhibitors and considered for coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); P2Y12 inhibitors (ticagrelor 91%, thienopyridine 9%) were stopped prior to CABG. The primary outcome was recurrent myocardial infarction or death following ICA and prior to revascularisation or decision for conservative management. 2 patients (0.8%) had recurrent MI and died following ICA and prior to planned CABG, demonstrating a small risk of MI and death in patients who have delays to CABG following ICA for ACS.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Improved Visualization of the Internal Branch of the Superior Laryngeal Nerve during Pharyngeal Endoscopic Subepithelial Dissection with Use of Red Dichromatic Imaging.
authors: Fujinaga Y, Tamada Y, Yamaguchi Y, Matsuura K, Kachi H, Oyama M, Mori H, Iwai S
abstract: Endoscopic subepithelial dissection is a minimally invasive treatment for superficial pharyngeal neoplastic lesions, requiring preservation of important neural structures such as the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (ibSLN). We report a case in which red dichromatic imaging (RDI) appeared to improve the visualization of a linear structure presumed to be the ibSLN compared with white-light imaging (WLI). A 57-year-old woman underwent endoscopic subepithelial dissection for a 5-mm superficial lesion on the pharyngoepiglottic fold. Both WLI and RDI revealed a whitish linear structure beneath the lesion, which was presumed to represent the ibSLN based on its anatomical location and course. The presumed nerve structure appeared to be more clearly delineated with RDI than with WLI before mucosal incision and remained identifiable after submucosal injection and during dissection. This enhanced visualization may have helped guide the selection of the mucosal incision line and dissection plane. En bloc resection was achieved without apparent nerve injury. No dysphagia, hoarseness, or other adverse events occurred postoperatively. These findings suggest that RDI may serve as a useful adjunct for visualization of the structure presumed to represent the ibSLN during pharyngeal endoscopic subepithelial dissection and may support nerve-preserving strategies.

title: Acute Pancreatitis Caused by Impaction of Migrated Surgical Staples in the Duodenal Papilla After Distal Pancreatectomy.
authors: Inaba K, Motomura M, Azuma Y, Kimoto T, Takahashi H, Ueo T, Narita R, Tada K
abstract: A 67-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy for pancreatic body cancer. On postoperative day (POD) 23, the patient presented with epigastric pain and was diagnosed with delayed peripancreatic fluid collection, which was treated with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage. On POD 51, the patient developed recurrent epigastric pain. Laboratory tests revealed elevated pancreatic enzyme and inflammatory marker levels. Computed tomography revealed acute pancreatitis and a high-density area in the duodenal papilla suggestive of a foreign body. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography revealed that the surgical staples were impacted in the minor duodenal papilla and were successfully removed. Although pancreatography did not demonstrate residual staples, three additional staples were subsequently removed from the pancreatic duct. Pancreatitis improved after endoscopic treatment, and the patient was discharged. This case suggests that the migration of staples used during surgery may be a contributing factor to postoperative pancreatitis.

title: A tunable brain-targeted PEGylated ginsenoside Rg1 derivative disrupts the ROS-mediated inflammasome-pyroptosis cascade to ameliorate Alzheimer's cognitive deficits.
authors: Zhu X, Liang H, Fan L, Bo J, Diao F, Qian Y, Zhang G, Li W
abstract: The pathogenic cascade of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and pyroptosis serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although ginsenoside Rg1 exhibits pleiotropic neuroprotective activities, its poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability severely hinders its clinical translation. To overcome this limitation, a brain-targeted delivery system was constructed using a covalent conjugation strategy, linking purified Rg1 with rhodamine B-modified polyethylene glycol (PEG) of varying chain lengths (Rg1s-PEG). After screening, the derivative Rg1s-PEG-600 was identified as achieving an optimal balance between hydrophilic stealth properties and steric hindrance, demonstrating enhanced brain accumulation and favorable biosafety profiles. In both in vitro and in vivo models of lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation, Rg1s-PEG-600 attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, inhibited canonical neuronal pyroptosis mediated by the NLRP1/3 inflammasomes, and significantly ameliorated behavioral deficits and synaptic loss. Furthermore, in chronic 5xFAD transgenic mice, systemic administration of Rg1s-PEG-600 for 12 weeks markedly reversed spatial memory decline, anxiety-like behavior, and synaptic protein depletion. Mechanistic studies further revealed that this targeted nanotherapeutic not only suppressed the ROS-NLRP1 signaling axis and subsequent neuronal pyroptosis in the AD brain but also comprehensively inhibited amyloidogenesis and Tau hyperphosphorylation. This work provides a promising, multitarget nanotherapeutic strategy to overcome BBB limitations and disrupt the complex pathological networks underlying neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Screening a thermotolerant Komagataella phaffii strain with methanol cross-tolerance and the associated physiological and transcriptional responses.
authors: Li C, Jiang T, Bo Y, Lu Z, Zhou Y, Zhang G
abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a prominent methylotrophic yeast widely used in industrial biotechnology for heterologous protein production, chemical synthesis, and C1 feedstock utilization. However, its industrial application is limited by thermal stress and methanol toxicity, while the relationship between heat adaptation and methanol tolerance remains poorly understood. Here, we obtained a thermotolerant mutant ATH through ARTP mutagenesis followed by adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) under heat stress (37 °C). ATH tolerated heat and methanol robustly under individual stress conditions, achieving 3-fold and 8-fold higher cell densities than GS115 at 37 °C or in 5% (v/v) methanol, respectively, yet failed under the combined stress of 37 °C and 5% methanol. Using three proteins (GFP, OPH, and ChiA) as reporters, we found that ATH showed higher heterologous expression than GS115 at 33 °C. Physiologically, ATH displayed enhanced cell wall/membrane integrity, reduced ROS accumulation and lower lipid peroxidation (>30% reduction in MDA), and accelerated formaldehyde clearance. Transcriptomics identified 561 shared differentially expressed genes, with coordinated upregulation of heat shock proteins (HSP70/40/90 families; Hsp104 and Hsp70-SSA2), antioxidant enzymes (catalase, peroxiredoxin), and cell wall/membrane remodeling genes, alongside downregulation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis. Whole-genome resequencing further distinguished ATH from GS115 by only 19 variants (9 SNPs and 10 InDels), highlighting a compact genetic basis for the evolved phenotype. This work provides a K. phaffii chassis with improved individual heat and methanol tolerance and elucidates the physiological, transcriptional, and genomic mechanism underlying heat-methanol cross-adaptation.

title: Liquid contactable colorimetric sensor array for bacteria discrimination.
authors: Kim YM, Lee MG, Kim SH, Shin DI, Lee JH, Kim J, Lim SH, Yi GR
abstract: Rapid and reliable detection of bacterial metabolites in liquid culture is critical for early diagnosis of sepsis, yet conventional dye-based colorimetric sensor arrays (CSAs) are hindered by dye leaching and poor interfacial interactions in aqueous environments. Here, we introduce a polydimethylsiloxane-based CSA (PDMS-CSA) platform that overcomes these limitations by leveraging the intrinsic hydrophobicity of PDMS to stably immobilize water-soluble indicator dyes within the polymer matrix. This design ensures direct, unimpeded contact between analytes and sensors, enhancing both sensitivity and reproducibility. The PDMS matrix further contributes by preventing dye leaching while facilitating mass transport of bacterial metabolites such as ammonia (500 μM), hydrogen sulfide (50 μM), and carbon dioxide (1.7 mM) to the immobilized indicators, thereby enabling rapid and robust colorimetric responses. Using this platform, we achieved reliable differentiation between cocci and bacilli within 3 h, demonstrating a capability for rapid, clinically relevant bacterial identification. By combining operational simplicity with high analytical performance in complex liquid media, PDMS-CSAs represent a transformative approach for point-of-care sepsis diagnostics. Beyond sepsis, this strategy offers a versatile framework for the development of next-generation, non-invasive microbial sensor operating platforms with broad translational potential in clinical and environmental monitoring.

title: Cold-induced transcriptomic responses are associated with strain-dependent Salmonella enterica persistence in refrigerated lettuce leaves.
authors: Rodríguez-Alvarez Y, González N, Araya MP, Moreno-Switt AI, Melotto M, Jacob C
abstract: Salmonella enterica is a leading cause of foodborne outbreaks linked to leafy greens. Refrigerated storage is a cornerstone of leafy-green safety, yet strain-level variation in the persistence of internalized S. enterica under these conditions remains poorly understood. Screening of eleven S. enterica strains revealed marked differences in their persistence within detached romaine lettuce leaves stored at 10 °C. Two isolates, belonging to serovars Montevideo and Newport, displaying contrasting persistence phenotypes were selected for detailed analysis, and these differences were confirmed at 4 °C. To investigate transcriptional responses associated with this variation, we profiled transcriptomic responses to cold stress in nutrient-rich medium by RNA-seq and evaluated post-cold recovery. Both isolates grew similarly at 28 °C but diverged at 4 °C, with the Montevideo strain maintaining higher growth capacity. Functional enrichment of KEGG pathways and Gene Ontology terms revealed shared repression of central metabolic and energy-producing pathways, coupled with induction of stress-response processes. Genes associated with general stress responses, cold-shock functions, and envelope integrity were more prominently represented among the induced responses of the Montevideo strain after cold exposure. These findings indicate that strain-dependent differences in Salmonella persistence during refrigerated lettuce storage are associated with distinct transcriptional responses to cold stress and post-cold recovery phenotypes observed in cultured bacteria. Consideration of strain-level variation may improve interpretation of pathogen persistence during leafy-green storage and inform future microbial risk assessments.

title: Behavioural avoidance to imagined conditioned stimuli in differential fear conditioning.
authors: Mitra S, Lyons AL, Hajiloo M, Greening SG
abstract: The underlying mechanisms of how a fear is born in our imagination is presently unclear. The current study used differential fear conditioning to assess how a fear is created in one's mind and how behavioural avoidance interacts with imagined fear. This study contained an Acquisition, Behavioural Avoidance, and Transfer phase. During the Acquisition phase, participants combined instructions such that whether they heard "imagine yellow" (colour instruction) or "imagine horizontal" (orientation instruction) they were to imagine yellow horizontal lines (CS+) and likewise for the "imagine blue" and "imagine vertical" instructions (CS-). Unbeknownst to participants, they only received the mild shock (US) to the orientation instructions. This manipulation allowed for a disambiguation of descriptive and depictive elements of how imagination interacts with fear. Next, participants completed the Behavioural Avoidance phase, whereby participants had the option to avoid the US after hearing the trial's instructions. Finally, in the Transfer phase, participants were visually shown the CS+ and CS- to determine how their fear transferred from imagery to perception. Self-report, skin conductance response (SCR), and behavioural avoidance attempts were used as dependent measures. Results from each phase and dependent measure suggested that fear was driven by the orientation instructions. Furthermore, fear was shown to transfer from imagery to the corresponding visual stimuli. In this way, these results suggest that both depictive and descriptive elements are involved in the creation of fears in our imagination.

title: Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) Mapping and Visualization of Pre-Implementation Determinants for Sepsis Care Transitions.
authors: You SB, Stawnychy MA, Song J, Hirschman KB, O'Connor M, Sang E, Oh S, Pitcher K
abstract: INTRODUCTION: High-quality care transitions are essential for sepsis survivors at risk of readmission and long-term complications. These complex innovations require coordination across organizations, individuals, and processes. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) offers a systematic approach to identifying multi-level implementation determinants, but translating them into actionable strategies remains challenging. This study examines the representation of implementation determinants across CFIR domains and visualizes their cross-domain interconnectedness. METHODS: CFIR-guided, semi-structured pre-implementation needs assessment interviews were conducted with stakeholders involved in sepsis care transitions across five hospital-home healthcare (HHC) dyads. Thirty-two themes identified through deductive-inductive coding were mapped to CFIR domains and constructs and visualized using node diagrams. RESULTS: Sixty-one interviews with 91 stakeholders identified 32 themes spanning all five CFIR domains, with most themes mapping to multiple domains. Access to Care theme mapped across all five domains, while External Policies and Incentives and Informal Caregiving themes were represented only once. Implementation Process domain was most represented and Innovation least represented. All constructs within the Implementation Process and Individual Characteristics domains were captured. Node diagrams illustrated the depth and interconnected influence of determinants in sepsis care transitions. CONCLUSIONS: Stakeholders identified complexity emerged across technical, structural, and policy domains as both an innovation feature and contextual determinants of sepsis care transitions. CFIR mapping and visualization provided a structured approach to characterizing pre-implementation complexity in sepsis care transitions. Examining determinant representation and cross-domain interconnectedness may help identify cross-cutting, potentially high-leverage implementation needs and inform strategy selection and tailoring for complex hospital-to-home interventions.

title: Associations between infection and organ age gaps: results from the UK Biobank.
authors: Shi Y, Wang M, Zhao S, Li J, Ye D, Sun X, Mao Y, Guo J
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infection may have lasting influences in multiple organ systems, but its associations with organ-specific biological age remain unclear. We aimed to examine associations between infection burden (IB) and organ age gaps. METHODS: Among 42,395 UK Biobank participants, qualifying infection diagnoses were identified from first occurrences data. The IB score was defined as the number of distinct infection diagnoses first recorded before baseline. Participants were classified according to whether at least one qualifying infection diagnosis had hospital inpatient data as its earliest-record source, and infections were grouped into eight predefined categories. Biological ages of 18 organs were calculated from plasma proteomics-based organ signatures, with higher organ age gap (OAG) indicating accelerated aging process. Linear regression and restricted cubic spline models were used to examine associations between infections and OAG. RESULTS: Higher IB score was positively associated with OAG of 12 in 18 organs. IB-OAG associations were statistically significant for hospital-treated infections, but not for non-hospital-treated only infections. Among eight infected subcategories, sepsis showed the strongest and most widespread associations with OAG. Associations between IB score and OAG of heart, kidney, and pancreas were significantly nonlinear. In addition, associations were generally stronger for infection diagnoses first recorded in more recent time windows and weaker for diagnoses first recorded further in the past. CONCLUSIONS: IB was associated with accelerated multi-organ aging, particularly for hospital-treated infections and sepsis. Our findings highlighted the critical roles of infection in organ aging, which provided clues to make tailored strategies for the prevention of aging related disorders.
